name: Weather Prime
description:
A polished, full-featured weather companion for your GNOME top bar. A clean pill shows current conditions at a glance; one click opens a rich drop-down with six tabs.

Now — temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind, and barometric pressure with a smart trend arrow that hints at incoming weather.
Hourly — 12-hour outlook with temperature, precipitation chance, humidity, and wind.
7-Day — daily highs and lows, precipitation, humidity, and wind.
Air — choose AirNow (US EPA AQI per pollutant), OpenWeatherMap (global 1–5 AQI plus all eight pollutants), or Open-Meteo PM 2.5 / PM 10, with automatic source fallback.
Astronomy — sunrise and sunset, moonrise and moonset, moon phase and illumination, powered by WeatherAI.io.
Map — live RainViewer precipitation radar over Esri satellite imagery; one click launches Windy, Zoom Earth, Ventusky, Weather.com, Wunderground, or NWS Radar for full interactivity.

Live NWS severe-weather alerts surface automatically for US locations. Location auto-detects via GeoClue2 or can be set manually with built-in city search — and the preferences page now updates the moment GeoClue moves you. The theme follows your system light/dark setting (or pin it), the panel can sit left/center/right at original or 1.5× size, and refresh cadence is independently configurable for weather, air quality, and radar.

Works out of the box — no API keys, no signup, no fees. Optional free keys from WeatherAPI.com, WeatherAI.io, AirNow, and OpenWeatherMap unlock the additional providers above whenever you want them.
